## The checker's report

Check of the design sheet for `claw-machine` (Claw Machine, band 4 to 6), round 1. File read: `games/claw-machine/ART.md` as checked, lines 1 to 179 (everything above `## The look`). Line numbers are lines of that file.

Records: all six exist; code, standing and check state are as the lookup prints today (2.5 department-published-foundation, K.MD.3 and 1.MD.4 state-board-adopted-standard, the three nl records curriculum-institute-guidance; all `confirmed`; no regime applies). The three California Summaries quoted are the pack's own text, and no web address is in the sheet.
Limits: every limit the sheet takes is in that record's Limits (none comes from "In a child's hands"), and what it marks as left open is left open there. One number in the records part is not fixed by the ladder table (finding 5).
Levels: levels, sub-bands, basis (us-ca official, nl convention), the cross-grade label at 5 and 6, the end-of-primary label at 4, 5 and 6, and "no gap" are as printed. One thing the levels imply is not said (finding 11). Headings are all there and in order; no position id names a grade, a groep or a level; the claim uses each standing's words and makes no attainment claim.

Not a sheet finding: the status block of `REFINEMENT.md` records only a hash of the sheet part. It must name the commit that holds the sheet as checked ("A pass names the text it judged").

Findings

1. **The band and its age rule, line 15** (ruling 4). "An older one the last" can be read as the last row of the ladder, which contradicts line 14. Replace the line with:
`- **`null`.** Starts at `two-colours`, the youngest default. The defaults are open-ended at both ends: a child of 4 or younger starts at `two-colours`, and a child of 6 or older at `colours-then-kinds`.`

2. **The toy, lines 24, 25, 26; The four mechanic questions, line 58.** The cable swings and the shadow is "under the claw", so where a drop lands, and which mouth is "nearest", would depend on the moment the finger lifts. Nothing may depend on when to tap. Replace:
 - Line 24: `- **While the finger slides**: the trolley follows, the cable swings against every change of speed, a soft tick sounds per stud of travel, and a round shadow straight under the trolley shows where the claw will land. The swing is for the eye and the ear only and never moves the shadow. Hard against either end of the rail the trolley hits a buffer brick and a bell rings.`
 - Line 25: `- **When the finger lifts**: the claw drops onto the shadow, straight under the trolley, however far the cable has swung, so where it lands never depends on the moment the finger lifts. It lands with a clack that squashes it, and closes. A toy under it is lifted with a pop while its neighbours hop in a ring that fades with distance; with nothing under it the jaws bite air, the claw bonks the studs and the whole tray rings. The hoist comes up through a rising ratchet roll, quicker and higher as it climbs.`
 - Line 26: `- **With a toy in the jaws**: the toy swings wider and slower than the bare claw, heavier for a big toy. Let go, it comes down on the shadow under the trolley, wherever its swing has carried it, clicks onto the nearest free studs with a squash, and its neighbours hop. Let go over another toy, it clicks on top and the two stand as a stack.`
 - Line 58, last sentence: `Nothing else asks for attention: a toy let go near the gobblers goes to the mouth nearest the point under the trolley, wherever the swing has carried it, so there is no aiming, and nothing is timed.`

3. **The object-by-action grid, lines 38, 39, 40.** Eight cells name a motion and no sound (stack with empty claw, stack with swing, gobbler with wait, all five ledge cells), so they cannot be said to sound different. Replace the three rows with:
 - Line 38: `| **A stack of toys** | Takes the top one only, with a pop pitched higher the taller the stack; the rest wobble and settle with a soft double click | The stack grows to three with a click a step higher than the last and sways; on a stack of three the toy bounces off and lands beside it with a boing | Too heavy on top: the stack teeters one way and comes down toy by toy, each clicking onto free studs with its own note | Goes down like dominoes in the direction of the swing, in a quick run of clacks from the first toy to the last | The cable winds itself up a creak at a time so the jaws clear the top |`
 - Line 39: `| **A gobbler** | Lifted by the stud on its head: the motor groans, its legs kick, its belly rattles; let go, it drops back into its own place. Each one takes the lift its own way | Its sort: one gulp, and the toy drops into the belly window on the others. Not its sort: a chomp, a freeze, the toy held out on the tongue beside its own body, then spat in an arc back to the tray | Its sort: three chomps with bulging cheeks and a swallow that can be followed down. Not its sort: cheeks bulge, eyes cross, and it sneezes the toy out and rocks back on its heels | Ducks the bare claw with a squeak and pops up again; snaps at a toy swinging past and misses with a clack of teeth | Opens wider and wider with a gargle that rises as the jaw drops, tongue out, feet pattering as it shuffles to stay under the claw. It does this for any toy: it finds out what it was given only by chewing |`
 - Line 40: `| **The ledge where the next ones wait** | While toys are on the tray: the one bonked ducks with a squeak, pops up further along with a cork pop, and shuffles back to its place. When the tray is clear: the claw hooks the gate with a clank and they come in ("The scenes") | Caught by one of them with a slap of hands and lobbed back onto the tray overarm with a falling whistle | Caught by all of them with one grunt, who stagger under it on pattering feet and heave it back together with a huff | They lean out of the way one after another, like grass, each with a soft creak a step higher than the one before | They stare up, heads following the sway in step, humming one note that slides up and down with it |`

4. **The object-by-action grid, after line 41.** Line 95 puts only the next crew of the same cycle on the ledge, so in a cycle's last sort, and in every one-sort cycle (the first four positions), no one is there and the five ledge cells have no result. Add as a new paragraph after the table:
`When no one waits on the ledge (a cycle's last sort, and every cycle with one sort), the ledge answers by itself: the empty claw rattles its gate, a small toy let go on it rolls down the gate bars with a run of pings and clicks onto the tray, a big one thuds on it and slides off with a scrape, a swing drags the claw tip along the bars like a comb, and a wait above it makes the gate creak open a crack and shut.`

5. **The designed order, line 87 (and the figure in line 154).** Line 154 says the fullest belly holds six, snack included. That holds only if the nine toys of `three-ways-wide` split five and four by size, and the table says "sizes mixed". Replace line 87 with:
`| `three-ways-wide` | three, in a changing order | 9 toys: one of each colour in each kind, five of one size and four of the other | the widest load, with three groups in two of its sorts |`

6. **The designed order, lines 91 and 105.** "Spat back" does not cover a wrong try with the size crew (the toy slides off a head or drops through the bars, line 66), so whether those count is not settled. Replace:
 - Line 91: `**How a cycle goes.** Only a toy's first let-go into a gobbler in each sort is looked at. With P such first tries in the cycle (toys times sorts) and M of them into a gobbler that does not take that toy, whichever way the toy comes back (spat out, slid off a head or dropped through the bars): the cycle went well when 6 × M is at most P, badly when 2 × M is at least P, and mixed otherwise. Well moves the position one step up, badly one step down, mixed leaves it; a visit put away before the cycle ends leaves it too. Nothing on screen shows the position or that it moved (pack: game-design, ordered-challenges-high-success.md).`
 - Line 105: `- `cycle.tried`: for each toy, whether its first try of this sort has been made, and `cycle.misses`: how many first tries of the cycle went into a gobbler that does not take that toy. Neither is ever shown.`

7. **The designed order, line 93.** The taller crate is said to hold visibly more at every step. By the table, the step to `two-kinds` and the step to `two-sizes` bring no more toys, kinds or crews (the second brings fewer). Replace the line with:
`**The harder option.** When a cycle has ended, two crates stand on the ledge: the next load for the stored position, and beside it a taller one holding what the next step up would bring. Its height marks it as the bigger job at every step. At most steps it also holds visibly more: more toys, more kinds of toy, or more crews riding on it. At the two steps that bring a new attribute and no more of anything (`two-kinds` and `two-sizes`) it is told apart by its height and by the crew riding on it, which goes by an attribute the stored position does not sort by. The child puts the claw on either. A taller crate that goes well moves the position that one step up; one that goes mixed or badly moves nothing, so choosing the harder load never costs a step. At `three-ways-wide` there is one crate.`

8. **The designed order, line 109** (ruling 5). Gobblers and waiting creatures are moved about (blown back a step, line 119; shot forward on landing, line 123; popped up further along the ledge, line 40). No field holds where they stand, and the sheet does not make the moves short-lived. Replace the sentence "The claw and a lifted gobbler are not saved: on load the claw hangs at rest and every gobbler stands in its place." with:
`The claw and a lifted gobbler are not saved: on load the claw hangs at rest and every gobbler stands in its place. A gobbler moved out of its place in any way (lifted, blown back a step, shot forward on landing) and a waiting one that ducked along the ledge are back in their own places within a moment, so nothing about where they stand is left to save.`

9. **The characters and their fixed tastes, line 128** (ruling 5). A snack stays in a belly for a whole sort and "never joins the load", so it is not in `cycle.toys`. Its other two properties are in no field, and the cycle's seed is not saved. Replace the paragraph with:
`Each gobbler arrives with one toy of its own sort already in its belly, its snack, so every group is begun and shown before the child adds to it. The snacks of one crew differ only in the attribute that crew goes by: each takes its other two properties from the first toy listed in `cycle.toys`, so a snack is rebuilt from the saved state and is not a field of it. A snack is the gobbler's own and never joins the load.`

10. **The scenes, line 141.** The sheet does not say what a first visit shows. The first showing's cause ("a crew comes in") has nothing that brings the first crew in, and a scene that played on first open before any touch would have no sound. Append to the paragraph:
`A first visit opens as an ended cycle does, with nothing to replay: the tray is bare, the saved state has `finished` set, an empty `cycle` and one entry in `crates`, laid out from the default position, and that crate waits on the ledge with its crew riding until the child puts the claw on it.`

11. **The records, us-ca, line 152** (pack: education, age-maps-to-levels-through-the-lookup.md and limits-come-from-the-limits-section.md). Sorting a second way rests on 2.5 alone, a `preschool-tk` record. The lookup does not return that level at age 6, where the default starts on `colours-then-kinds`, and the sheet does not say so. Replace the line with:
`  Limits taken: one attribute and two or more groups at the earlier age; at the later age a second attribute may be taken as a second step, so no sort asks a child to hold two attributes at once. Left open by Limits: which attributes. Colour, kind and size are the game's own choice. This foundation belongs to `preschool-tk`, which the lookup returns at ages 4 and 5 and not at 6: for a six-year-old, sorting the same toys a second way rests on a record of the level below the levels returned for that age, and on no `kindergarten` or `grade-1` record.`

12. **The records, nl, after line 167** (ruling 7). The claim and "Where the two differ" say the second sort rests on us-ca alone, but no sentence under the nl heading says no nl record is named for that part. Add as a new line after line 167:
`No nl record is named for sorting the same toys a second way: the three records above speak of sorting by one property, or by one or more characteristics, and none speaks of sorting a set again.`
